plan: This is a second-price auction where the winner pays the second-highest bid. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the weakly dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of what others bid. Bidding above value risks paying more than the item is worth to me if I win against a bid between my value and my bid. Bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my private value of $31.

This is a second-price auction where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid, so bidding above my value adds risk of overpaying relative to my value without benefit, and bidding below reduces my chances of winning profitable auctions. With no history to inform deviations from theory, I'll bid exactly my value of $31 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price auction where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. Since I win and pay the second-highest bid if I have the highest bid, there's no benefit to bidding above or below my true value of $46. Bidding exactly $46 ensures I win whenever the item is worth more to me than the price I'd pay, and I never overpay since I only pay the second-highest bid, not my own bid.
